description_full: Unicaja Banco, S.A. engages in the retail banking business in Spain. The company offers current, savings, young person, and payment accounts; term deposits; debit, business, and credit cards; mortgages; study, eco-mobility, mobility vehicle, reform, and home loans; and home, car, health, accident, funeral, company and agro uni, company health, SME and retail damage, corporate liability, agricultural, and life insurance products. It also provides pension plans; investment funds; bill and tax payment, and collection management services; payments; POS products; short-term and medium/long-term financing; ATM, foreign trade facility, and currency management and exchange services; and private and personal banking services, as well as digital and mobile banking services. The company was founded in 1991 and is headquartered in Málaga, Spain.

financial_summary: UNICAJA BANCO S.A.U. is a mid-cap financial services business with a $7.8B market cap on $2.3B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +9% over the past three years, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
The company is burning through $1.7B of cash, and without positive owner earnings any valuation rests on hope rather than evidence.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year.

Management returns a meaningful 5.1% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 56% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.
